title: Flyway
subtitle: HPAI Control Area, Checkpoints & Depopulation

brief.userPrompt: Tuesday October 20, 2026, a cold clear morning during fall waterfowl migration. Prairie Gold Turkey Cooperative's company veterinarian Dr. Anders Whitfield sampled the Larkin Ridge Turkey Complex (four barns, 62,000 tom turkeys, complex manager Brett Sandoval) on Monday after two days of rising mortality and a drop in water consumption. The exercise starts at 07:50 when the Minnesota Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory reports an H5 presumptive positive and the Minnesota Board of Animal Health calls Calder County Emergency Management Director Marcus Lindqvist. Plan clocks start at the presumptive result. Players: the Director, Deputy Director Alina Petrova (Operations), Sheriff Dale Rademacher, County Public Health Director Naomi Eshleman, PIO Colette Marsh, the Prairie Gold biosecurity manager Gretchen Oyelaran. The SimCell plays Extension Educator Jonah Kettering. Timeline and pressure points: quarantine of the infected premises within 4 hours; control area (3 km infected zone, 7 km buffer, 10 km control area, 10 km surveillance zone, to be confirmed against the Minnesota plan) set within 8 hours, and the team must decide whether the epidemiology section should widen it because two other Prairie Gold premises share the same catch crew; the first four of 11 checkpoints staffed by hour 3 and all 11 by hour 8, with the Sheriff short of deputies and mutual aid from Pell and Ritter counties; 24-hour depopulation goal for four barns with limited crews, foam or carbon dioxide chosen by the incident management team, and a power failure at barn 3; disposal: on-farm composting is not possible at the site, the Calder County Regional Landfill (Rhys Tolliver, 120 tons per day) would take the carcasses if the Minnesota Pollution Control Agency approves, and a queue of trucks builds past 12 hours, pushing loads to Pell County Landfill; 11 premises hold market-age toms that must move within 14 days, the Dunmore processing plant (410 employees) is outside the control area, and the Larkin feed mill inside it needs a permit; a premises that is at-risk must not be moved to monitored until the Board says so; permit requests pile up (feed to barns with 4 to 6 days of feed left, a load of finished birds, a rendering truck, egg carriers) and the service target is 24 hours; the 4-H and county fair board ask about a poultry swap meet on Saturday and 190 small flock owners need messages; 37 barn workers entered the infected barns and County Public Health must arrange 10 days of monitoring and antiviral prophylaxis through the Minnesota Department of Health, with a language barrier among catch crews; a grocery distributor and an export broker call the cooperative before the state has published anything; social media claims that eggs and turkey are unsafe; the producer notice, the state release and the consumer message must carry identical counts and distances; the county Board of Commissioners considers a county emergency declaration and the Director considers asking the state for National Guard support at checkpoints; the farm family loses a flock and needs same-day contact. Decisions the exercise should record: order a quarantine, establish the control area, change a premises designation, issue or deny movement permits, set the depopulation order and method, choose a disposal site, request federal resources, request an emergency declaration, publish a producer and consumer notice, record depopulation complete and samples taken. Measures: time from presumptive positive to quarantine and to control area; depopulation within 24 hours; premises sampled by their due date; permits decided in time and unaffected premises able to move; disposal sites chosen without a backlog; message consistency across the state, industry and public health. The SimCell plays the Minnesota Board of Animal Health (state veterinarian and permit coordinator), USDA APHIS Veterinary Services (area veterinarian in charge), the Minnesota Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory, the Minnesota Pollution Control Agency, the Minnesota Department of Health, state emergency management, the cooperative's growers and plant manager, the landfill, neighboring counties, a grocery distributor, reporters and residents.
constraints: Every email address of the county uses the exercise domain caldercountymn.example; the cooperative uses prairiegoldturkey.example; outside parties use fictional domains; never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.

Distances, intervals and zone names are labeled as the federal plan's planning values with the Minnesota plan governing; premises are a code plus a fictional farm name; counts, distances and times agree across every order, permit, letter and press release; presumptive results come from the network laboratory before the national reference laboratory confirms.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; the Minnesota Board of Animal Health, USDA APHIS, the diagnostic laboratory, the Pollution Control Agency, the state health department, state emergency management, growers, the landfill, neighboring counties, buyers, reporters and residents are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: Beating the plan clocks that start at the presumptive result, supporting the state's animal health decisions without making them, moving unaffected birds and feed under permit, and keeping one set of numbers across the state, the cooperative and the county.
overview.threat: Highly pathogenic avian influenza, carried into Calder County by wild waterfowl during the fall migration, has infected the Larkin Ridge Turkey Complex (IP-1; four barns, 62,000 tom turkeys). Before STARTEX, on Monday, Prairie Gold Turkey Cooperative veterinarian Dr. Anders Whitfield sampled the flock after two days of rising deaths and falling water use. At 07:50 on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, a cold, clear morning, the Minnesota Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory reports an H5 presumptive positive, and the Minnesota Board of Animal Health calls Director Marcus Lindqvist. The national reference laboratory has not yet confirmed the result. The outbreak threatens the county's other 47 commercial turkey premises, including two Prairie Gold premises that share IP-1's catch crew. It also threatens the Larkin feed mill inside the planned control area, the Dunmore processing plant outside it, and roughly 190 small flocks.
overview.operationalImpact: From 07:50 the county EOC in the Public Safety Building Training Room runs against the Annex K clocks. The Board's quarantine on IP-1 is due by 11:50 and the first four checkpoints must be staffed by 10:50. The full control area and all 11 checkpoints are due by hour 8, and the 24-hour depopulation goal arrives through injects that move the clock forward. The federal plan's planning values are a 3 km infected zone, a 7 km buffer and a 10 km surveillance zone, and the Minnesota plan governs. Players must decide whether to ask the Board's epidemiologists to widen the zone because of the shared catch crew. Sheriff Rademacher does not have enough deputies for the checkpoints, so he asks Pell and Ritter counties for mutual aid while the Director weighs a request for National Guard support. Barn 3 loses power during depopulation, so county generators and the Larkin Fire District water tanker go to the site. The incident management team chooses between foam and carbon dioxide while crews are short and capped at 10-hour shifts. Composting is not possible on the farm. The Calder County Regional Landfill can take 120 tons a day but needs Minnesota Pollution Control Agency approval, and after 12 hours a line of trucks forces loads to Pell County Landfill. Permit requests pile up against a 24-hour service target: feed for barns with 4 to 6 days left, a load of finished toms, a rendering truck and egg carriers. On 11 premises, market-age toms must move within 14 days, and an at-risk premises cannot be shown as monitored until the Board says so. County Public Health must reach 37 barn workers, some of them catch-crew members who do not speak English, for 10 days of monitoring and antivirals through the Minnesota Department of Health. A grocery distributor and an export broker call the cooperative before the state has published anything. Social media claims that eggs and turkey are unsafe. The fair board asks about Saturday's poultry swap meet, and the farm family needs contact the same day.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to meet the Annex K 4 clocks from the 07:50 presumptive result: open the EOC at Level 2 within 60 minutes, confirm the IP-1 address, barn count and access roads before the Board's 11:50 quarantine, and staff the first four checkpoints by 10:50 and all 11 by hour 8.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to support the Minnesota Board of Animal Health's decisions without making them: send the shared catch-crew evidence to the Board's epidemiologists for a decision on widening the zone, route disputed permits through the permit coordinator under CCACMP 8, and decide on Pell and Ritter mutual aid, a National Guard request and a county emergency declaration under CDSDSL 10.

objectives.name: Logistics and Continuity
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to keep IP-1 depopulation and disposal moving: send county generators and the Larkin Fire District tanker when Barn 3 loses power, staff crews on shifts of 10 hours or less, escalate when the landfill queue passes 12 hours, and help process feed, finished-tom, rendering and egg-carrier permits for unaffected premises within the 24-hour service target.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to keep one set of counts, dates and distances across the Board, the cooperative and the county by issuing the 12-hour producer and consumer notice with the state, answering the social media claims that eggs and turkey are unsafe, coordinating replies to the grocery distributor and export broker, and reaching all 37 barn workers in a language they understand.

roles.name: County Emergency Management Director
roles.team: Team A: County Emergency Management Director
roles.description: Manages the county EOC as a supporting node to the Board and USDA APHIS unified command, serves as county liaison to the state, and owns escalation, mutual aid, National Guard and emergency declaration decisions.
standingOrders: Support, Don't Decide: quarantine, zones, premises designations and depopulation method belong to the Board and APHIS, so carry evidence to them and never announce an animal health decision for them.
Clock Discipline: every Annex K target runs from the 07:50 presumptive result, so report slippage early instead of hiding a missed clock.

Escalate on Triggers: when the landfill queue passes 12 hours, a checkpoint goes unmanned for more than 2 hours or a responder is injured, call the state EOC, and review the county declaration at every 16:00 planning meeting.
Ask Before Acting Alone: request mutual aid or the Guard through the state EOC, and do not stand up county-only zones or roadblocks.

roles.name: Deputy Director / Operations
roles.description: Manages the EOC floor, the IP-1 site liaison, logistics for staging at the fairgrounds, generators, water, crew welfare and the permit desk seat alongside the Board's permit coordinator.
standingOrders: Field Over Screen: if the status board and the site liaison disagree, trust the site and correct the board.
Worker Limits: crews work shifts of at most 10 hours with no 12-hour night shifts, even if that means depopulation falls behind the 24-hour goal.
Keep Commerce Moving: unaffected premises run under permit, so push feed and egg-carrier requests to the permit coordinator and never close the sector on the county's say-so.
Report Up Fast: call the Director the moment a CDSDSL 10 escalation trigger is met.

roles.name: Sheriff (Checkpoint Commander)
roles.description: Manages the 11 control area checkpoints, traffic control on the boundary roads and security of IP-1, working with the County Highway Engineer.
standingOrders: Priority Roads First: staff the roads that carry turkey, feed, shavings and rendering traffic first, and get four sites up by 10:50.
Permit Is the Pass: let a vehicle through only with a valid Board permit and cleaning and disinfection, whatever its driver says.
No Gaps Over Two Hours: flag a checkpoint early if it might go unmanned, and request Pell and Ritter mutual aid before you run out of deputies.
Security Without Spectacle: protect IP-1 and the crews without naming the farm or family to the public.

roles.name: County Public Health Director
roles.team: Team D: County Public Health Director
roles.description: Manages follow-up of exposed workers, symptom checks at the staging area and antiviral prophylaxis with the Minnesota Department of Health for every person who entered the IP-1 barns.
standingOrders: Reach Every Worker: contact all 37 barn workers, including catch-crew members, through interpreters as needed, and do not count a worker as reached until they understand the message.
Ten Days From Last Exposure: run daily monitoring for 10 days after each person's last exposure, and restart a worker's clock if they reenter the barns.
Health Over Speed: no crew member enters without PPE and a symptom check, even under depopulation pressure.
Protect Privacy: share worker health data only with the Minnesota Department of Health, never with the cooperative or the PIO.

roles.name: Public Information Officer
roles.description: Manages county consumer and producer notices, rumor control and social media response in coordination with the Board's public information officer and the cooperative.
standingOrders: Board Numbers First: never announce the size of the control area before the Board does, and keep counts, dates and distances identical across every notice.
No Names: no notice names a farm, a farmer or a worker.
Truth Over Reassurance: say eggs and poultry are safe when handled and cooked properly and that the risk to the public is low, and do not promise anything the state has not confirmed.
Reconcile Before Replying: when the state and the cooperative publish different numbers, call the Board's PIO before answering any reporter.

roles.name: Prairie Gold Turkey Cooperative Biosecurity Manager (Industry Liaison)
roles.description: Owns cooperative biosecurity, access to IP-1 for depopulation, tracing of the shared catch crew, member permit requests and continuity of the feed mill and Dunmore plant from the EOC industry liaison seat.
standingOrders: Disclose the Contacts: give the Board's epidemiologists the catch crew's schedule and every premises it visited now, even if that may widen the zone and hit members.
Continuity Under Permit: ask for movements of feed, toms and eggs through the permit coordinator, and never move birds on an informal nod.
One Set of Numbers: hold the grocery distributor and export broker until the state has published, then use the state's counts.
Status Is the Board's: never describe an at-risk premises as monitored until the Board says so.

phases.title: The Presumptive Call
phases.goal: Tests whether the EOC acts on an unconfirmed H5 presumptive positive and starts the Annex K clocks at 07:50, without waiting for Ames confirmation or making animal health decisions that belong to the Board.
beats: (07:50) The Minnesota Board of Animal Health calls Director Marcus Lindqvist to report an H5 presumptive positive from the Minnesota Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory on the Larkin Ridge Turkey Complex (IP-1; four barns, 62,000 tom turkeys). The SimCell stresses that the national reference laboratory in Ames has not confirmed it. Under Annex K 3, the EOC must open at Level 2 in the Public Safety Building Training Room by 08:50.

The Board asks the county to confirm the IP-1 address, barn count and access roads so the quarantine can be issued by 11:50. Complex manager Brett Sandoval and County Highway Engineer Pete Vasquez give road details that conflict, so Deputy Director Alina Petrova has to reconcile them.
Noise item: the Highway Department reports a routine detour for a culvert repair on a county road. It has nothing to do with IP-1 access, but it lands in the same inbox.

Biosecurity Manager Gretchen Oyelaran starts the Prairie Gold plan 4 actions. Trucks leaving IP-1 are stopped, the crew on site is logged and dispatch manager Ruth Calloway's team has 4 hours to produce the 14-day trace list. Early dispatch notes show that two other Prairie Gold premises shared IP-1's catch crew last week.

First outside questions: a contract grower asks whether today's feed delivery from the Larkin mill can go ahead. Extension Educator Jonah Kettering forwards the fair board's question about Saturday's poultry swap meet.

phases.title: Drawing the Lines
phases.goal: Tests whether players can set up the first checkpoints and the control area on the federal planning values with the Minnesota plan governing, send the catch-crew evidence to the Board's epidemiologists, and get one first public message out before rumors set the story.
beats: Time jump to (10:20). The Board sends its draft control-area map to the EOC. It shows the federal plan's planning values (3 km infected zone and 7 km buffer, with a 10 km surveillance zone beyond them) and says the Minnesota plan governs. The map puts the Larkin feed mill inside the control area and the Dunmore plant outside it. The first four checkpoints are due by 10:50, and Sheriff Dale Rademacher reports that he can staff only three.

The trace list arrives from Ruth Calloway's team and confirms the shared catch crew at two Prairie Gold premises. Players have to send this evidence to the Board's epidemiologists for a decision on widening the zone. They must not redraw the zone themselves or label those premises as contact premises.

Red herring: a resident posts that turkeys are dying at the Prairie Wind complex, and a reporter repeats it as a 'second outbreak.' Complex manager Lena Halvorsen reports normal mortality and normal water use there, and no sample has been submitted. The EOC needs to correct the post without overstating what is known.

Social media posts claim that eggs and turkey from Calder County are unsafe to eat. A reporter from a fictional regional paper calls PIO Colette Marsh for comment with a 12:00 deadline. Communications lead Ivan Petrescu tells the EOC that a grocery distributor and an export broker have already called the cooperative, before the state has published anything.

The Board asks the county to confirm the staging area at the Calder County Fairgrounds west lot (CDSDSL 5), with state hand-wash and shower trailers due within 12 hours. It also wants the IP-1 road details locked in before the 11:50 quarantine order.

phases.title: Holding the Perimeter
phases.goal: Tests the exercise's one decision point and whether IP-1 depopulation stays on schedule under resource strain. It also tests whether responders and barn workers are protected under Annex K 8.
beats: Time jump to (15:30). All 11 checkpoints are due by hour 8 (15:50), and the Sheriff is still short even with Pell and Ritter county deputies arriving under mutual aid. DECISION POINT: the Director must decide whether to ask for National Guard support and declare a county emergency under CDSDSL 10. Asking means escalating and drawing public attention. Not asking means unstaffed checkpoints overnight and the risk of uncontrolled traffic through the control area.

Barn 3 at IP-1 loses power during depopulation, and its fans and lights go down. Players have to send the two 30 kW county generators and the Larkin Fire District's 4,000-gallon tanker (CDSDSL 5) and work out who directs their use at the site.

The incident management team reports it is choosing between foam and carbon dioxide while crews are short and capped at 10-hour shifts. The Board asks whether the county can provide lodging (the 40-room Larkin motel block) and meals from the Larkin Lutheran Church kitchen for the 18:30 meal.

Public Health Director Naomi Eshleman must reach 37 barn workers for 10 days of monitoring and antivirals through the Minnesota Department of Health. Several catch-crew members do not speak English, and the cooperative's contact list is incomplete.

The 12-hour producer and consumer notice is due with the state by (19:50). Its counts, zone distances and times must match the Board's order and the cooperative's grower call. Meanwhile the IP-1 farm family asks for someone to contact them today.

phases.title: Queues and Permits
phases.goal: Tests whether players can keep disposal and permitted movements on track against the 24-hour targets, keep premises designations within the Board's authority, and finish the day with one reconciled set of numbers and a path toward recovery.
beats: Time jump to Wednesday (05:30). Landfill Manager Rhys Tolliver reports that the truck line at the Calder County Regional Landfill (120 tons a day, pending Minnesota Pollution Control Agency approval) has passed 12 hours. Players have to escalate and coordinate rerouting loads to Pell County Landfill through checkpoint routes.

Permit requests have piled up against the 24-hour service target: feed for barns with 4 to 6 days left, a load of finished toms for Dunmore, a rendering truck and egg carriers. Disputed requests go through the permit coordinator under CCACMP 8. A grower demands that the EOC list his at-risk premises as 'monitored,' and players must refuse until the Board says so.

The Dunmore plant and the Board weigh whether to keep processing birds from unaffected premises. Market-age toms on 11 premises must move within 14 days, and welfare and space limits begin around day 10 (Prairie Gold plan 4).

(07:50) The 24-hour depopulation goal arrives, and the national reference laboratory confirms H5. The SimCell checks whether the bird counts, distances and checkpoint numbers in the county situation report match the Board's order and the cooperative's records, and puts one discrepancy in front of players to reconcile.

Players look ahead to recovery: cleaning and disinfection inspected by APHIS, the cooperative's 8–12 week estimate to restocking (Prairie Gold plan 9), and the Annex K 9 demobilization steps (checkpoints removed within 24 hours of the control-area release and the after-action meeting within 30 days). The exercise then ends (ENDEX).

objectiveCapabilities.why: Players must run the Annex K clocks from the 07:50 presumptive result: open the EOC at Level 2 within 60 minutes, confirm IP-1 address, barns and access roads for the Board's quarantine order, and support the Board and APHIS control area.
The Sheriff must staff the first four of 11 control-area checkpoints by 10:50 and all 11 by hour 8 with too few deputies, putting turkey, feed, shavings and rendering roads first.

The Director must send the catch-crew evidence to the Board and leave zone decisions to it. He also has to decide on mutual aid, a National Guard request and a county emergency declaration through the state EOC.
Disputed and urgent movement permits must go through the Board's permit coordinator at the permit desk. The county must not decide or close anything on its own authority.

The Barn 3 power loss, the depopulation water need and crew lodging and meals test delivery of the county generators, the Larkin Fire District tanker, the staging lot, the motel block and the church kitchen.
Keeping IP-1 depopulation on track for the 24-hour goal and clearing the landfill queue for carcass disposal exercise the depopulation-support and disposal steps.
Feed, finished-tom, rendering and egg-carrier permits for unaffected premises have to move through the permit desk within the service target.

Players must issue the 12-hour joint producer and consumer notice, answer the egg and turkey safety rumors and the '10 miles' claims, and keep one set of Board counts and distances without naming the farm.
All 37 exposed barn workers, including the Spanish and K'iche' speakers in Catch Crew C, must be reached for antiviral prophylaxis and 10-day symptom monitoring.

hotwash.methodDescription: Ask the room for three things that went well and three that broke or failed during the response. Go around the room one team at a time (county EOC, sheriff and checkpoints, cooperative, communications), write each item on the whiteboard in two columns, and don't debate items until every team has spoken.

questions.text: At I-02, the Board asked you to confirm IP-1's address, barns and access roads by 09:30. The complex manager said the CR 12 drive was the only way in. The County Highway Engineer said loaded trucks had been using an ungated field lane off 230th Street. Whose answer did you send to the Board, when did you send it, and who put a checkpoint or gate on the 230th lane? Did you treat the engineer's reply as evidence that changed the quarantine order, or as a side note in an email thread? Under Annex K 3, the clocks started at 07:50. Which of them did you actually meet?

At I-14 (10:15), the state EOC told you that tonight you would have 11 checkpoint sites and about 4 people. They also said a Guard request with a county declaration had to reach them by noon to get soldiers there around 18:00. Did you decide on the declaration and the Guard request before noon? If not, what stopped you? When the commissioners chair warned that reporters would ask for the farm name, who decided what could be said? Did you keep that call with the Board and the cooperative, or did the county end up answering it?

At I-07b, Pell could send two deputies starting at 11:30, Ritter could send nobody until tomorrow, and the Pell deputies had never run an ag checkpoint. Who briefed them on what a Board permit looks like, where the cleaning and disinfection station is, and what PPE to wear? How did you staff the first four checkpoints by 10:50 without putting anyone on a shift longer than 10 hours? What would have had to be ready before this morning for you to fill the night shift?

At I-05, a Facebook post with 84 shares claimed that every turkey within 10 miles was being killed and that eggs and turkey were unsafe. Meanwhile, a 60-vendor poultry swap meet was going ahead unless someone official said otherwise. What did you tell the public, and the fair board, while the result was still only presumptive? Who decided about the swap meet: the Board or the county? Did the county, the cooperative and the Board all use the same counts and control-area distance, or did each one put out its own numbers?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Minnesota Board of Animal Health duty veterinarian (the hazard authority), speaking for the Board/USDA APHIS unified command; can transfer to the Board epidemiologist, quarantine officer or permit coordinator
simcellScripts.trigger: A player calls the Board duty line (651-555-0188) to ask it to widen the zone because of the shared catch crew, to tag 'Cottonwood Bend' and 'Willow Slough' as contact premises, to move North Fork to monitored, to release the feed permits, or to ask which access points go into the quarantine order.
hardQuestions: You want me to widen the zone or tag premises? On what evidence? Send my epidemiologists the load sheets, the GPS, the dates and the missing cart C&D record in writing. A dispatcher's question at the bottom of an email isn't a designation request, and your EOC board doesn't designate anybody.
My quarantine order is due by 11:50 and it still lists one access point. Is the 230th Street lane a controlled gate in the order or not? I need the county's answer in writing, with who staffs it.
North Fork tested negative, so the grower wants 'monitored'? That's an at-risk premises. Only the Board moves it, and only on the Board's schedule. Who put that idea on your status board?
Your SITREP says the control area is 10 miles. My order says 10 km. Which number are you putting in front of reporters?
concessions: Once the written catch-crew trace reaches Board epidemiology, the epidemiologist calls back within the hour with the Board's designation for both premises, and may widen the zone. The county repeats the Board's call and does not make its own.
Once the county confirms the 230th lane as a staffed, barricaded controlled gate, the quarantine order goes out with both access points before 11:50.

Once the county corrects its SITREP to the Board's numbers (one premises, 62,000 birds, 10 km control area, 11 checkpoints), the Board puts all three parties on one consistent line in the joint notice, and the permit coordinator works the oldest requests (PR-1014, PR-1019) first.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Minnesota Homeland Security and Emergency Management state EOC duty officer in St. Paul (state emergency management), with the Pell County Sheriff's Office duty sergeant Halvorsen on the mutual aid side
simcellScripts.trigger: The Director or the Sheriff calls the state EOC about National Guard support for checkpoints, state-funded mutual aid or a waiver on hauling hours, or the Sheriff calls Pell or Ritter County to chase more deputies.
hardQuestions: Do you have a county emergency declaration from the Board of Commissioners on file? The Governor's office normally wants it with the request. If it reaches me by noon, the earliest arrival is about 18:00 tonight. After that, tomorrow afternoon at best.

What exactly is the mission? How many sites, how many soldiers per site, which shifts, where do they report, who briefs them on a Board permit and the C&D station, and who supplies their PPE? I can't send 'help with checkpoints.'
Have you used up local and mutual aid? Your own numbers show 4 deputies, 2 from Pell until 19:30 and none from Ritter. Is that in writing?
You're asking me for more depopulation crews and indemnity? That's not mine and not yours. The Board asks APHIS for that.
concessions: With a signed declaration and a written mission (sites, shifts, reporting point, briefing lead), the state EOC moves the request to the Governor's office and holds a target arrival of 18:00.
Pell's sergeant keeps his two deputies past 19:30 on the night shift if Calder sends a written checkpoint brief, permit samples and PPE to meet them at the fairgrounds west lot.
The state EOC starts work on a hauling-hours waiver for the carcass and feed trucks once the county sends route and load numbers that match the Board's permits.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Minnesota Department of Health zoonotic diseases epidemiologist (worker health and antiviral prophylaxis)
simcellScripts.trigger: County Public Health calls MDH about the 8 unreached Catch Crew C workers, the K'iche' speakers, getting oseltamivir to the staging area, the Prairie Gold HR request for a list of workers on Tamiflu, or adding depopulation crews to monitoring.
hardQuestions: You called the crew lead in Spanish and he said they 'understood'? Four of them speak K'iche'. Who interpreted, and did anyone pick up medication? No? Then they haven't been reached.

Three phones are disconnected and two people are listed by first name only. Where does Crew C sleep and where does their bus park? Have you asked the cooperative and the crew's contractor for that today?
Prairie Gold HR wants to know who is on Tamiflu so they can schedule shifts. You're not sending that, are you? What will you tell them?
Every depopulation crew member who enters a barn today starts a new 10-day clock. Who logs them at the staging gate before they go in?
concessions: Once the county names a meeting place and time (the crew bus or the staging area), MDH arranges a K'iche' interpreter through a language line and courier-delivers oseltamivir there.
MDH gives the county one answer for the employer: health information stays with Public Health and MDH, and HR gets only fit-for-duty or not-fit-for-duty notices.
Once the county runs the staging-gate symptom check and the entry log, MDH adds the depopulation crews to the tracker and runs monitoring for 10 days after last exposure.

Pell's scale house takes up to 8 loads, but only with a Board movement permit for each load and a set route. Has anyone asked the permit desk? Which checkpoint do they leave through, and does that route use the 230th lane?

MPCA here: I'll sign when I have the cell location, the cover plan and the daily tonnage in writing. Has the county sent it?

We're hearing about a second farm at Prairie Wind. People saw a trailer full of dead birds. Can you confirm or deny for the noon cut-in?

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. Capabilities, plans and procedures are being evaluated, not individual players or agencies.
The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. Players should not challenge the presumptive result, the herd details or the timing of the injects.

Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures, including Calder County Annex K, the CCACMP and the CDSDSL. Where a plan is silent or a value must be confirmed against the Minnesota plan, players say so and describe what they would do.

The Minnesota Board of Animal Health and USDA APHIS make all animal health decisions, including quarantine, control-area size, premises designations, movement permits and the depopulation method. County players discuss how they support those decisions, not how they would make them.
Players use the information available at the start of each module and the injects as they arrive. Players should not assume they know about events that have not been reported to the room.
All participants are treated as experts in their own roles and speak openly about gaps, constraints and workarounds.
artificialities: Time jumps between modules: Module 2 starts at 08:50 and Module 3 at 09:50 on Tuesday, October 20. Module 4 jumps overnight to 05:30 on Wednesday, October 21. Events between modules are summarized on facilitator Time Jump Cards.

The SimCell plays everyone outside the room. This includes the Minnesota Board of Animal Health, USDA APHIS, the state incident management team, the Minnesota Department of Health, state emergency management, the Minnesota Pollution Control Agency and the national reference laboratory in Ames. It also plays the Pell and Ritter county sheriffs, the landfills, the electric co-op, Prairie Gold staff not present, the growers, the media and the public.

Systems named in the plans are referenced but not touched. These include the PG-BIO-2026 dispatch system, the Board's premises and permit board, the county situation reports and the Annex K Appendix 2 checkpoint plan. No real orders, permits, declarations or resource requests are issued.

Phone calls, radio traffic, emails, social media posts, wire alerts and memos are delivered on paper or on screen. Players say out loud how they would respond instead of contacting real agencies or posting publicly.
Prairie Gold Turkey Cooperative, Calder County and the named premises, people and media outlets are fictional. Real agencies appear only as outside parties played by the SimCell.

modules.narrativeMd:
**Module 1: The Presumptive Call (07:50–08:50, Tuesday, October 20, 2026)**

It is 07:50 on Tuesday, October 20, 2026. It is a cold, clear fall morning in Calder County: 29°F at the Larkin airport, a light northwest wind and no precipitation. Fall waterfowl migration is at its peak, and residents are posting photos of large flocks of geese and ducks on the sloughs north of Larkin.

The county EOC in the Public Safety Building Training Room is dark, and status is normal, with no active incidents. Highway crews are on routine fall maintenance, and the Sheriff's day shift has six deputies on patrol. Prairie Gold's Larkin feed mill and its Dunmore processing plant (410 employees) are running normal Tuesday schedules.

On Monday, cooperative veterinarian Dr. Anders Whitfield sampled a flock after two days of rising deaths and falling water use. Nobody in this room has heard the result yet.
keyIssues: Whether to act on a presumptive laboratory result without waiting for confirmation from Ames
Starting the Annex K clocks at the moment of the presumptive result, not at the time of the phone call
Confirming premises address, barn count and every access road before the Board's quarantine order
Keeping county actions within support roles while the Board holds animal health authority
Answering early rumors and producer pressure before any official message exists

**Module 2: Drawing the Lines (08:50–09:50, Tuesday, October 20, 2026)**

It is 08:50, one hour after the presumptive result. At 07:50 the Minnesota Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory reported an H5 presumptive positive at the Larkin Ridge Turkey Complex: four barns, 62,000 tom turkeys. The Board calls it IP-1, with the public name "Ridgeline Farm". Ames has not confirmed and is not expected to report before tomorrow.

The EOC is open at Level 2 in the Training Room. The Board wants the IP-1 address, barn count and access roads confirmed, but the email thread disagrees. The complex manager reports one entrance off CR 12. The Highway Engineer reports that the CR 12 bridge has been posted at 10 tons since August and that loaded trucks use an ungated field lane off 230th Street. Separately, CR 31 closes at 09:00 for a three-day culvert job.

Prairie Gold has accepted the hold at IP-1, and nine people are logged on site. Its preliminary trace shows that contract Catch Crew C (11 workers) loaded at IP-1 on October 14, then worked at Cottonwood Bend and Willow Slough. A grower with four days of feed wants a yes or no on his delivery. A Facebook post saying every turkey within 10 miles will be killed and people should avoid eggs and turkey has 84 shares, and the fair board plans to hold Saturday's swap meet.

At 08:44 the Board sent DRAFT v1 of the control-area map, marked NOT FOR PUBLIC RELEASE. It shows a 3 km infected zone and a 7 km buffer zone, using federal planning values, with the Minnesota plan governing. The draft puts the Larkin feed mill inside the buffer zone, about 6 km from IP-1. The first four checkpoints are due at 10:50, but the Sheriff has deputies for only three sites.

**Module 3: Holding the Perimeter (09:50–10:50, Tuesday, October 20, 2026)**

It is 09:50, two hours after the presumptive result. The Board's quarantine order on IP-1 "Ridgeline Farm" is in draft, waiting on the 230th Street lane question. Three checkpoint sites are staffed on CR 12 and the two feed routes out of the Larkin mill. The fourth site is due at 10:50 and still has no deputy. Pell County's two deputies arrive at 11:30, and Ritter County cannot send anyone until Wednesday's day shift.

The USDA APHIS area veterinarian in charge and a state incident management team are setting up at the Calder County Fairgrounds west lot. The state hand-wash and shower trailers will arrive no later than 20:50. The first depopulation equipment trucks are inbound on the 230th Street lane. Trace list v1 confirms that Crew C used the same bus and catching cart at IP-1, Cottonwood Bend and Willow Slough. Crew C members also entered IP-1 barns 1 and 2, and the full trace list is due at 12:20.

Calls are coming in faster than the Training Room can log them. Social media and Northland 9 News are asking about a 'second outbreak' at Prairie Wind. The Prairie Ledger and Prairie Gold's grocery and export contacts are all waiting for numbers. The Annex K clocks are still running. The quarantine order is due at 11:50, the control area and all 11 checkpoints at 15:50 and the producer and consumer notice at 19:50. Every IP-1 barn must be depopulated by 07:50 Wednesday.

**Module 4: Queues and Permits (Wednesday, October 21, 2026, game time 05:30–08:30)**

It is 05:30 on Wednesday, October 21, 21 hours 40 minutes after Tuesday's 07:50 presumptive result. Overnight, the Board issued its quarantine order on IP-1 "Ridgeline Farm" and published the control area: an infected zone of 3 km and a buffer zone of 7 km, making a 10 km control area. The Board used the federal planning values, with the Minnesota plan governing.

The crews finished barns 3 and 1 on Tuesday. The second shift started at 22:00 and finished barn 2 at 04:40. Barn 4 is in progress, with completion projected at about 08:00, which is also when the second shift reaches its 10-hour cap. All 11 checkpoint sites were staffed through the night, but Site 9 ran on a single deputy from 01:00 to 05:00.

Carcass trucks have been lining up at the Calder County Regional Landfill since Tuesday evening, and the Minnesota Pollution Control Agency approval is still unsigned. The permit desk has 23 requests open, and 9 of them are older than 18 hours. The 24-hour depopulation goal arrives at 07:50. The national reference laboratory in Ames has still not reported.
